item.title: The optimal four-dimensional lattice quantizer and bounds from Voronoi facets
item.description: arXiv:2611.00100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the root lattice $D_4$ uniquely minimizes the normalized second moment among four-dimensional lattices, up to similarity. The computer-assisted proof combines the classification of secondary cones with integration over Voronoi cells and weighted sums of squares. In dimensions at least two, comparison with circular cones gives a lower bound in terms of the number of Voronoi facets, improving the sphere bound and recovering the hexagonal value in dimension two. We prove Ajjanagadde's circular-cone concavity conjecture and deduce the lattice case of his conjectured quantization bound.
item.dc:creator: Tianle Liu

item.title: Upper bounds for packings of cylinders around the unit sphere
item.description: arXiv:2611.00251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note we study the problem of packing infinite circular cylinders tangent to the unit sphere. For a given number of cylinders $N$, $N\geq 3$, the maximal common cylinder radius $R_N$ is the maximum $R$ for which there exist $N$ circular cylinders of radius $R$ with non-overlapping interiors, all tangent to the unit sphere. In 1990, Kuperberg conjectured that there does not exist a packing of more than 6 cylinders of radius one tangent to the unit sphere, that is, $R_7<1$. This conjecture was recently confirmed by an exhaustive computer-assisted case analysis. Here we prove new bounds for $R_N$ for small $N$ by considering an auxiliary configuration of spherical quadrilaterals. In particular, we provide a short geometric proof of Kuperberg's conjecture and show that $R_7<0.9978$.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Glazyrin

item.title: A sharp plank theorem for cube annuli
item.description: arXiv:2611.00379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a conjecture of Andr\'as Bezdek on plank coverings of square annuli. A plank in a Euclidean space is the closed region between two distinct parallel hyperplanes, and its width is the distance between them. Let $Q$ be a unit square and let $H$ be a square of side length $1/2$ whose sides are parallel to those of $Q$. Then every finite family of planks covering $Q\setminus H$ has total width at least $1$. More generally, if an axis-parallel box with side lengths $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ is removed from the unit cube in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\sum_jh_j = d-1$, then every finite plank covering of the remaining set has total width at least one. The bounds are sharp.
item.dc:creator: Egor Bakaev, Alexander Polyanskii

item.title: Promotion and Extension of General Escape-Covering Duality Relationship
item.description: arXiv:2611.00569v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bellman's lost-in-a-forest problem, Moser's worm problem, Lebesgue's universal covering problems, and the classical 'fits and covers' questions can be organized by a common obstruction principle: an object fits a region if some admissible group action places it in the region, whereas an escape object is one for which every placement fails to remain in the interior. In this paper, we develop a general theory of escape-covering duality for any dimension and explore several applications. For convex translation covers of all closed planar curves of Euclidean length one, we prove $ W \ge f(\sqrt3/9)+c_1>0.15545785378555,c_1=0.000009944944227372... $ Here $f(\sqrt3/9)$ is Wetzel's classical lower bound. For a rational polytopal Minkowski gauge and prescribed rational facet directions, we express universal closed-loop cover feasibility as a rational polyhedron in the facet offsets. After removing translations, minimum volume is attained at a vertex. Refining the facet directions gives explicit two-sided rational bounds for the unrestricted fixed-gauge worm constant. Four exact benchmarks recover known sharp values. The construction uses an elementary circuit--circumradius form of the established non-fitting-polygon and capacity theory. We supply its support and ledger derivation, the finite complete test family in arbitrary dimension, a cover vertex bound, and the resulting algebraicity statement. The surrounding escape--covering framework includes endpoint placement, attainment, gauge stability, and finite-to-continuum error bounds. For nonsymmetric gauges the objects are parametrized closed curves, so orientation-dependent length is retained. Through the published capacity identity, the improved Wetzel estimate gives a product volume--capacity factor below $1.023781939711102$ for every planar ellipsoidal gauge.
item.dc:creator: Zhipeng Deng

item.title: When Pedal Shapes Come Back: a Complex Story
item.description: arXiv:2611.01247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Under the usual nondegeneracy assumptions, repeatedly projecting a fixed point onto the side lines of an $n$-gon returns its shape after $n$ steps. We explain this classical theorem through a short complex-number identity: the multipliers of one step move cyclically around the polygon. The same calculation allows a different common angle of projection at each step. A sharp angle-dependent contraction bound identifies the incircle centre as the maximiser for tangential polygons. In space, even a regular tetrahedron can fail to recover its shape after four steps. We give an exact example, then show how concentric inscribed and circumscribed spheres restore a two-step return. Rectangular boxes provide a further four-step family.
item.dc:creator: Micha\l{} Zwierzy\'nski

item.title: A Banach--Stone-like Theorem for Slowly Oscillating Functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every lattice isomorphism between the lattices of slowly oscillating real-valued functions on proper metric spaces induces a coarse homeomorphism. This yields a Banach--Stone-like theorem for slowly oscillating functions, as well as a representation theorem for linear lattice isomorphisms between these function lattices. Both theorems were previously established by the author under the assumption of chain-connectedness. The present paper establishes both results for arbitrary proper metric spaces.
item.dc:creator: Yutaka Iwamoto

item.title: Optimal asymptotic bounds for design curves on manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.01895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A spherical $t$-design is a finite set of points on the $d$-dimensional unit sphere such that averaging any polynomial of degree at most $t$ over these points gives its exact spherical average. We study the corresponding notion for curves, where point averages are replaced by normalized arclength integration. For fixed $d\ge 2$, the length of such curves is known to be bounded below by a positive multiple of $t^{d-1}$ as $t\to\infty$. We show that this asymptotic order is attained: for every $d\ge 2$, there exists a constant $C_d>0$ such that, for every positive integer $t$ and every prescribed length $L\ge C_dt^{d-1}$, there is a simple spherical $t$-design curve of length $L$. This establishes the analogue for curves of the theorem of Bondarenko, Radchenko, and Viazovska, which resolved the Korevaar-Meyers conjecture for spherical design points. More generally, we prove the corresponding result on closed, connected Riemannian manifolds of dimension $d\ge 2$, where eigenfunctions of the Laplace-Beltrami operator substitute for polynomials. The proof combines a geometric construction of curves with continuously adjustable local lengths and an application of Brouwer's degree theorem.
item.dc:creator: Martin Ehler

item.title: Improved lower bounds for the kissing number in dimensions 49 to 61
item.description: arXiv:2611.01906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give explicit kissing configurations in R^d for every d = 49, ..., 61. The lower bound is improved over the best previously published value in all thirteen dimensions, by margins from 232 to 159,220 points and by 506,461 points in total. The configurations are obtained from the antipodal block lift of Yang et al. applied to the 52,416,000-point minimal shell of the extremal even unimodular lattice P_48p, using a class of 7,193 minimal lines and, in each dimension, a kissing configuration of R^k (k <= 15) with the largest available number of antipodal pairs. Two ingredients are new. The published class of 7,077 lines is grown to 7,193 by local search in three stages, as a sequence of exchanges between candidate lines and class lines; and the point count, which equals 52,416,000 + 2S + 2t with t the number of antipodal pairs and S the size of the union of t isometric images of the class, is maximised as a maximum-coverage problem by greedy search with iterated local search over pools of 4,000 automorphic images, reaching 92-100% of the trivial bound 7,193t. All results are verified in exact integer arithmetic, and the certificates are distributed with the code. Code and data: https://github.com/dimkadimon/KissingNumbers
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Kamenetsky

item.title: Rational barycentric coordinates and low degree adjoints
item.description: arXiv:2611.02110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study rational generalized barycentric coordinates (rational GBCs) on polytopes. We recall their essential theory and clarify some statements from the literature. We study polytopes that admit GBCs with low degree denominators (and hence, low degree (affine) adjoint polynomials). We give a full classification of polytopes that admit polynomial barycentric coordinates (i.e. constant adjoints).
item.dc:creator: Martin Winter, Tom Baumbach

item.title: Generalized Quasi-Symmetric Nets: A Constructive Approach to the Equimodular Elliptic Type and to Flexible $m \times n$ Nets
item.description: arXiv:2611.02229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quadrilateral meshes that flex with rigid planar faces are of interest to transformable architecture, rigid-foldable origami, and mechanical metamaterials. Their building blocks are flexible $3 \times 3$ nets, that is, Kokotsakis polyhedra with a quadrangular base, classified by Izmestiev. We study one of his types, the equimodular elliptic type, defined by three conditions on the flat angles, the third of them through Jacobi elliptic functions. We turn these conditions into equivalent algebraic ones, free of elliptic functions, which lead to the generalized quasi-symmetric nets (GQS-nets), polyhedra of this type that include the known elliptic quasi-symmetric nets. For every polyhedron of this type, we give a flexible polyhedron with the same flat angles and its flexion in closed form. From the simplest GQS-nets, we assemble arbitrarily large flexible $m \times n$ nets. Examples include nets that, at one position, form letters; further nets in the supplementary materials form digits or, seen along their rows, approximately follow the side silhouettes of a bunny and a fish. Unlike numerically computed mechanisms, these nets are exactly flexible. As an application, we design three such nets as transportable arch halls of 80 mm sandwich panels, which fold to fit through the door of a standard container or into the well of a low-bed semi-trailer, and we check them numerically under snow load and build a 1:20 model of one. Supplementary Mathematica notebooks verify the symbolic computations, a Python tool constructs the nets and checks them numerically, including for self-intersections, and further scripts recheck the halls.
item.dc:creator: Abdukhomid Nurmatov, Florian Rist, Jonathan Klein, Dominik L. Michels

item.title: On the dichotomy of $p$-walk dimensions on metric measure spaces II
item.description: arXiv:2611.02422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a volume doubling metric measure space endowed with a family of $p$-energies such that the Poincar\'e inequality and the capacity upper bound with $p$-walk dimension $\beta_p$ hold, for $p$ in an open interval $I\subseteq(1,+\infty)$, we prove the following dichotomy: either $\beta_p=p$ for all $p\in I$, or the function $p\mapsto \frac{\beta_p}{p}$ takes values in $(1,+\infty)$ and is strictly decreasing on $I$. Moreover, if the metric measure space is $d_h$-Ahlfors regular, we prove the following dichotomy: either $\beta_p=d_h+p-1$ for all $p\in I$, or the function $p\mapsto \frac{\beta_p-d_h}{p-1}$ takes values in $(-\infty,1)$ and is strictly increasing on $I$.
item.dc:creator: Meng Yang

item.title: Conformal dimension of Bedford-McMullen carpets
item.description: arXiv:2611.03252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the Hausdorff dimension of a Bedford-McMullen carpet with non-uniform fibres can be lowered with a quasisymmetry, provided that the defining iterated function system does not have a full column. We prove this by constructing explicit dimension lowering metrics which are quasisymmetrically equivalent to the Euclidean metric.
item.dc:creator: Roope Anttila

item.title: Open problems from the Length Optimization event at MDS 2026
item.description: arXiv:2611.03403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: During the Minisymposium on Length Optimization as part of the International Conference "Mathematics Days in Sofia - 2026", the participants collected the following open problems: 1. Find any non-trivial upper and lower bounds for the degree of a branching point in the Gilbert-Steiner problem with cost-function $c(x) = x^p$ in the metric space $X = \mathbb{R}^d$ for large $d$ and fixed $p > 1/2$ (see Section 1). 2. Determine whether a typical trajectory of a given branched optimal traffic plan has bounded length. To find the optimal transport plan between the Dirac measure in the center of a circle and the Lebesgue measure on the circle (see Section 2). 3. To find the maximal distance minimizers for any explicit compact sets (see Section 3). 4. What is the minimal $C$ such that for any set of $n$ points in the three-dimensional unit cube, there is a tour through all these $n$ points with the sum of the cubes of its edge lengths at most $C$ (see Section 4). 5. To explore parallels between tropical caustics and Steiner trees: do caustics really need convexity (see Section 5).
item.dc:creator: Yana Teplitskaya

item.title: On the second smallest ideal right-angled hyperbolic four-polytope
item.description: arXiv:2611.00118v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The regular ideal right-angled 24-cell has volume $4 \pi^2/3$ and is the unique minimum-volume entirely ideal right-angled hyperbolic four-polytope. We prove that the next distinct volume is $8 \pi^2/3$ and that its unique equality case is the reflection double of the 24-cell across one octahedral facet. We also show that an entirely ideal right-angled four-polytope whose facets are regular ideal octahedra or their doubles across triangular faces decomposes into a chain of regular 24-cells, with opposite cutting facets in each intermediate cell.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Kolpakov

item.title: Noncritical multi-bubbles and hyperbolic double bubbles
item.description: arXiv:2611.00252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that standard $k$-bubbles uniquely minimize perimeter in $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb S^n$ for $n\ge2$ and $1\le k\le n$, and that standard double bubbles uniquely minimize perimeter in $\mathbb H^n$ for $n\ge3$. For nonnegative curvature, the proof combines the structure and spectral theory of Milman--Neeman with a uniform semialgebraic exceptional set, an almost-everywhere profile comparison, and localized variational arguments. A curvature-variable lift gives a uniformly elliptic comparison at the Euclidean limit. The independent hyperbolic argument uses the rotational structure of Cotton--Freeman, a scalar meridian force potential, and a transverse conformal variation. The critical range $k=n+1$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb S^n$, and hyperbolic clusters with more than two finite cells, are not covered.
item.dc:creator: Zihao Wang

item.title: A Note on the NP-Hardness on Quadratic Optimization over Doubly Stochastic Matrices and the Gromov-Wasserstein Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.00479v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Gromov-Wasserstein problem is an extension of the regular optimal transport problem that is adapted for pairs of distributions residing in incomparable spaces. Broadly speaking, given a pair of metric measure spaces, the Gromov-Wasserstein problem seeks couplings between these spaces that minimize the distortion between the metric evaluations. In this note we record the fact that the Gromov-Wasserstein distance between finite metric spaces is NP-Hard to compute. Our argument relies on a reduction from the Hamiltonian Cycle Problem, and it builds on ideas in Vayer's thesis and Ryner et. al's work that draw connections between the 2-Gromov-Wasserstein and the Quadratic Assignment Problem. During the preparation of this manuscript we learned of the appearance of Breitung et. al's work, whose result essentially supersedes ours. We hope this note serves as a useful companion whose proof is, hopefully, more elementary and easier to understand.
item.dc:creator: Yong Sheng Soh

item.title: Markov-driven self-similar measures and non-homogeneous slicing
item.description: arXiv:2611.00962v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the concept of Markov-driven self-similar measures, a notion that simultaneously generalizes classical self-similar measures, self-conformal measures, dynamically driven self-similar measures and many random measures. This class is also closed under Cartesian products and linear projections. We initiate the study of this class of measures and investigate the $L^q$ dimension of Markov-driven self-similar measures under certain Diophantine conditions. As an application, we obtain the first Furstenberg slicing type results for intersections of Cantor sets in non-homogeneous settings.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Shmerkin, Shunsuke Usuki

item.title: Contact multiplicity and a sharp six-map bound for collinear self-similar dendrites
item.description: arXiv:2611.01291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K\subset\mathbb{C}$ be the attractor of $n\ge2$ similarities $z\mapsto\lambda z+b_k$, $0<|\lambda|<1$, whose fixed points are evenly spaced on a line, and suppose that $K$ does not lie in a line. We prove that $K$ can be a dendrite only if $n\le6$, and that such dendrites exist for every $2\le n\le6$; no separation or finite-intersection hypothesis is imposed. Hence, for $n\ge7$, every connected $K$ of this kind has interior points or separates the plane. Neighboring pieces of $K$ meet in similar copies of a single contact set. In a dendrite exactly one first-level piece meets this set, whereas for $n\ge7$ at least $n-\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil\ge2$ do, a bound attained by explicit quadratic parameters. The proof combines a planar translation obstruction for replicated contact arcs with an estimate based on Jensen's formula. After normalizing to $z\mapsto t+z/c$, $t\in\{-n+1,-n+3,\ldots,n-1\}$, the connectedness locus is the closure, outside the unit disk, of the roots of monic integer polynomials of height at most $n-1$. The same estimate shows that, for $n\ge7$, every such polynomial with a non-real root $c$ satisfying $|c|^2\ge\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil+1$ has subleading coefficient of absolute value at most $\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$, and that this bound is sharp. Accordingly, for $n\ge7$, at every non-real boundary point $c$ of the locus with $|c|>1$, each expansion $c=\sum_{j\ge0}d_jc^{-j}$ with integer digits $|d_j|\le n-1$ has $|d_0|\le\lceil2\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$.
item.dc:creator: Bernat Espigule

item.title: Dimension bounds for finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2611.01795v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter polytope has dimension at most $81$, substantially improving Prokhorov's bound of $995$. A refinement of Prokhorov's method gives the intermediate bound $162$, while an extension of Vinberg's planar-angle comparison to the finite-volume setting yields the sharper bound. Both arguments combine improved weighting functions with estimates using cusp geometry to control weight contributions of angles at ideal vertices or edges incident to them.
item.dc:creator: Lizi Guo, Fangting Zheng

item.title: An affine reverse Faber-Krahn inequality via information decay
item.description: arXiv:2611.02279v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ admits $S\in\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{R})$ such that $\lambda_1(SK)|K|^{2/n}\le Cn$, where $C$ is universal. For origin-symmetric bodies of volume one, the bound holds in maximal Gaussian measure position. The main step is the spectral estimate \[ \lambda_1(D)\le C(P)\bigl(n+\sqrt{n I(\nu\mid\gamma_n)}\bigr) \] for an even isotropic log-concave probability measure $\nu$ supported on a symmetric convex body $D$, with Poincar\'e constant at most $P$ and finite relative Fisher information. A second-order Stein estimate and an information jump under convolution give entropy decay faster than $m^{-1}$ for normalised sums. Their supports control the Gaussian measure of dilates, and a Brownian bridge expansion gives the spectral estimate. A Gaussian-weighted ground state supplies a measure whose Fisher information is bounded in terms of $\lambda_1(K)$. The square-root dependence then gives the bound of order $n$.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Colbrook, George Stepaniants

item.title: Convexity of Radial Mean Bodies via an Extension of Ball's Bodies
item.description: arXiv:2603.14134v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we extend a classical theorem of Keith Ball on integrals of log-concave functions along rays against the weight $r^{p-1}$ to the previously inaccessible regime $p\in (-1,0)$: if $g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+$ is an integrable, upper semi-continuous, log-concave function which attains its maximum at the origin and has the origin in the interior of its support, then \[ x\mapsto \left(\frac{p}{g(o)}\int_{0}^{\infty}r^{p-1}(g(rx)-g(o))\mathrm{d}\,r\right)^{-\frac{1}{p}} \] is a gauge on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Our approach also provides a new proof of the original regime $p> 0$. The argument is based on a reduction to a two-dimensional inequality derived from Pr\'ekopa's theorem, which may be of independent interest. As a consequence of this extension, we resolve a nearly 30-year-old question of Richard Gardner and Gaoyong Zhang in the affirmative. In 1998, R. Gardner and G. Zhang introduced the radial $p$th mean bodies $R_p K$ of a convex body $K\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ for $p>-1$. Furthermore, they established that $R_p K$ is convex for $p\geq 0$, but the convexity of $R_p K$ for $p\in (-1,0)$ remained open. We prove that $R_p K$ is convex for all $p>-1$.
item.dc:creator: Dylan Langharst

item.title: The lattice covering density of the regular octahedron
item.description: arXiv:2609.23210v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the lattice covering density of the regular octahedron is $9/8$, establishing the optimality of the classical body-centered cubic covering. A hypothetical lattice covering of smaller density would yield a lattice basis whose six Kuhn tetrahedra each fit in a translate of the octahedron. A sharp determinant bound then gives a contradiction. As a consequence, the maximum order of an undirected Abelian Cayley graph with three generators and their inverses and diameter at most $k$ is $\frac{32}{27}k^3+O(k^2)$ as $k\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Yanlu Lian, Fei Xue

item.title: Quasiconformal uniformization and extension for planar trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.14236v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A quasiconformal uniformization theorem of Rickman from 1966 asserts that every bounded turning planar arc is the image of the unit segment under a quasiconformal self-map of the plane. We prove an analogous uniformization theorem for planar trees by showing that every planar quasiconformal tree with uniform branch separation is quasiconformally equivalent to a quasiconvex planar tree with uniform branch separation and Hausdorff dimension arbitrarily close to 1. Along the way, we show that every quasisymmetric (resp. bi-Lipschitz) homeomorphism between planar quasiconformal trees that respects the counterclockwise orientation of the branches at every branch point can be extended quasisymmetrically (resp. bi-Lipschitz) to the whole plane. As a corollary of the extension theorem we construct a class of quadrivalent quasiconformal trees, which includes the Vicsek fractal, so that each tree in this class is the Julia set of a uniformly quasiregular map of $\mathbb{R}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Fotis Ioannidis, Vyron Vellis

item.title: Equidistant Affine Subspaces: Explicit Bounds, Structural Reductions, Transverse Products, and Fixed-Codimension Stability
item.description: arXiv:2610.37421v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{N}(k,n)$ be the largest size of a family of affine $k$-planes in $\R^n$ at pairwise separation distance one. We develop a unified treatment of upper bounds, dimension reduction, product constructions, and fixed-codimension stability. Orthogonal-projection coordinates give a rank-stratified distance identity; a Veronese lifting converts its polynomial consequences into simultaneous total isotropy. Connected Nash decomposition and an analytic diagonal argument yield an explicit bound \[ \mathcal{N}(k,n)\leqslant 2^{\,2^{\,3(k+1)(n-k)}}. \] For configurations whose direction sums have dimension at most $k+1$, we prove the exact reduction $\mathcal{N}_{\leqslant k+1}(k,n)=\mathcal{N}(1,n-k+1)$. Every codimension-two configuration splits off a common linear factor, so $\mathcal{N}(n-2,n)=\mathcal{N}(1,3)$. A transverse product construction gives multiplicative inequalities. We further prove that for every fixed codimension $c$, the sequence $\mathcal{N}(k,k+c)$ is eventually constant. In codimension three, a sharper normal-span argument gives \[ \mathcal{N}(k,k+3)=\mathcal{N}(7,10)\qquad(k\geqslant7), \] where the numerical threshold uses the computer-assisted theorem $\mathcal{N}(1,3)=7$. The structural and stability results are otherwise independent of that numerical input.
item.dc:creator: Jia Li

item.title: Petty's equilateral-set conjecture in dimension five
item.description: arXiv:2610.39967v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Petty conjectured that every n-dimensional real normed space contains n+1 equidistant points. The conjecture was proved in dimensions three and four by Petty and Makeev, respectively. We prove the five-dimensional case: every five-dimensional real normed space contains six equidistant points. The proof uses a bordism of equilateral configurations and a homological obstruction.
item.dc:creator: Kaiwen Yang

item.title: A nonstandard analysis approach to limit operators and Fredholmness in Roe-like algebras
item.description: arXiv:2412.08130v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $(X,d)$ be a uniformly locally finite metric space, and $T$ an operator in the uniform Roe algebra $C_u^*(X)$ (or uniform quasi-local algebra $C_{ql}^*(X)$). In this paper, we introduce the concept of limit operators of $T$ on galaxies in the nonstandard extension of $X$, and prove that $T$ is a generalized Fredholm operator with respect to the ghost ideal in $C_u^*(X)$ (or $C_{ql}^*(X)$) if and only if all limit operators on afar galaxies are invertible, and their inverses are uniformly bounded. In particular, if $X$ has Yu's Property A, then $T$ is a Fredholm operator if and only if all limit operators on afar galaxies are invertible. Using techniques in nonstandard analysis, our result strengthens a work of \v{S}pakula--Willett \cite{SpW} on the characterization of Fredholmness by using less limit operators.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Guo, L., Qian, J. and Wang, Q. (2026), A nonstandard analysis approach to limit operators and Fredholmness in Roe-like algebras. Bull. London Math. Soc., 58: e70534
item.dc:creator: Liang Guo, Jin Qian, Qin Wang

item.title: Quantum error-correcting codes from aperiodic monotiles: the Hat and the Spectre
item.description: arXiv:2607.15326v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Li and Boyle showed that the Penrose tiling defines a quantum error-correcting code: superpositions of tilings over isometry orbits protect quantum information against erasure of any bounded region. We extend the construction to the aperiodic monotiles discovered by Smith, Myers, Kaplan and Goodman-Strauss. For the Hat, we prove strong local indistinguishability for all Hat tilings, and we prove local recoverability unconditionally for all nonsingular Hat tilings via the torus parametrization of the underlying cut-and-project scheme. The remaining singular case reduces to one sharply posed geometric question -- can a region that is a union of hats be retiled a second way? -- which we verify computationally has no counterexample up to a substantial scale: a certified $2490$-tile patch admits precisely one tiling by hats, so all $2^{2490}$ of its tile-subregions retile uniquely. Unlike the Penrose, Ammann-Beenker and Fibonacci tilings, both monotiles form two local-indistinguishability classes, so their code spaces split into two erasure-correcting sectors carrying a superselected classical label. Whether the label survives depends on which isometries are gauged: the Spectre's classes are exchanged by a $30^{\circ}$ rotation and merge once all proper isometries are gauged, whereas the Hat's are exchanged only by reflections. Under the physically natural gauge group $SE(2)$, the Hat code therefore stores one robust classical bit -- the handedness of its long-range order, readable in any bounded window with separation $\Delta = |K|\sqrt{5}/3$ -- alongside its protected quantum sectors. It is the reflexible monotile, not the chiral one, that carries the chirality bit. We give the exact Perron-Frobenius data of both codes, including the per-class reflected-Hat frequencies $(3\mp\sqrt{5})/6$ and the Spectre orientation-class frequencies $(5\pm\sqrt{15})/10$.
item.dc:creator: Josep Batle, Adam Bednorz

item.title: On Riemannian Geometry in Elastic Diffeology
item.description: arXiv:2608.01037v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Blohmann's tangent functor makes the category of elastic diffeological spaces a Cartesian tangent category in the sense of Cockett and Cruttwell. We use this structure to develop Riemannian geometry on elastic diffeological spaces. Following Cockett and Cruttwell, with additional axioms for scalar multiplication, we introduce connections, covariant derivatives and curvature; for a Riemannian metric we prove a Koszul formula and the uniqueness of the Levi-Civita covariant derivative. Our main result is a variational characterization of geodesics: if a full connection whose vertical part is Levi-Civita admits a geodesic flow fixing the zero section, then the critical paths of the energy functional are exactly the paths satisfying the geodesic equation, and regular length-minimizing paths are geodesics after constant-speed reparametrization. On elastic spaces for which the real line is a curve object, completeness of the geodesic spray yields such a flow and uniqueness of geodesics. The results apply to quotients of complete Riemannian manifolds by free isometric actions of countable groups, such as irrational tori, and, under a tangent-commuting hypothesis, to mapping spaces from a closed manifold into elastic spaces for which the real line is a curve object, including free loop spaces of complete Riemannian manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Yusuke Shiobara

item.title: Uniformly Bounded Orthonormal Bases of Homogeneous Polynomials on the Complex Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.14160v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We resolve the long-standing problem of Rudin concerning uniformly bounded orthonormal bases of homogeneous polynomials on complex unit spheres. Specifically, we show that for every $K \geq 2$ and $N \geq 0$ there exists a basis of degree $N$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^K$ that is orthonormal with respect to the surface measure of the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^K$ and uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on $K$ on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^K$. Bourgain resolved the case $K = 2$ in 1985 and the case $K = 3$ in 2016. No cases $K \geq 4$ were previously known.
